name: Home
tagline: A zero-cost smart-home dashboard: LPUs post sensor readings to ThingSpeak, and a GitHub Pages page charts them against the forecast.
about: A personal monitoring stack built around LPUs (Local Processing Units): field devices that each carry a few sensors and post to their own ThingSpeak channel over HTTPS. The first is a Campbell CR310 logging two rainwater tanks and a rain gauge; a Raspberry Pi with an RTL-SDR (rtl_433, for a 433 MHz weather station), a Pi camera and an ESP32 mushroom house are planned. It borrows the flood network's habits (Campbell loggers called LPUs, a Pi with an RTL-SDR) but shares no code or data with Flood-Net, which neither absorbed nor replaced it.

status.summary: Live with one LPU (the CR310 on the tanks and rain gauge); last change 16 Oct 2026 put tank water in and out on one chart.
next: Bring the Pi + RTL-SDR weather-station LPU online (rtl_433 to ThingSpeak)
Add the Pi camera LPU's time-lapse stills
later: Close the control loop through ThingSpeak TalkBack queues

components.name: Dashboard
components.what: One self-contained page: stat tiles, tank volumes and days till empty, charts, forecast vs actual, a CRUD for collections.

components.name: CR310 LPU program
components.what: CRBasic: tank levels, rain accumulation, battery and panel temperature, HTTPPost every 5 minutes.

components.name: Weather-station bridge
components.what: Pi script: rtl_433 JSON from a 433 MHz station, aggregated and posted to ThingSpeak.

components.name: Camera publisher
components.what: Pi script: captures a still, updates manifest.json, prunes and git-pushes it for the dashboard.
